method: COMPILED FROM 2 SOURCES. S1: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW '4427 Bladder/Urothelial locally advanced or metastatic enfortumab vedotin and pembrolizumab (eviQ ID 4427, version 1)' (first approved 5 November 2025; review due 31 December 2026), 23 claims; LICENCE: CC BY-NC 4.0. eviQ also states that its content should not be hosted on external sites, and that commercial entities must contact eviQ to seek permission (https://www.eviq.org.au/copyright). Adaptations must cite the eviQ ID, version and URL. (read at https://www.eviq.org.au/copyright (Disclaimer and copyright page)). S2: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from Spanish Society of Medical Oncology (SEOM) and Spanish Genitourinary Oncology Group (SOGUG), Clinical and Translational Oncology 27(11):4142-4159 (doi 10.1007/s12094-025-04045-2) 'SEOM–SOGUG clinical guideline for urothelial cancer (2025)' (published 17 September 2025), 10 claims; LICENCE: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (read at Europe PMC fullTextXML <license> element for PMC12559142). Verify each source separately: verify.py --source <file> --only-source S<n>. Edition 2.0 keeps every eviQ 4427 claim (S1) unchanged and adds S2, the SEOM–SOGUG 2025 national society guideline (international, CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, paraphrased), for where enfortumab vedotin with pembrolizumab sits among the other first-line options (platinum chemotherapy, avelumab maintenance, nivolumab with cisplatin-gemcitabine, single-agent checkpoint inhibitors) and for later-line sequencing. S2's graded recommendation tables were stripped; claims come from its narrative. ESMO's 2024 interim first-line update (Annals of Oncology) has no open copy and SITC's 2021 urothelial guideline predates the EV-302 trial, so neither was used.

claims.claim: **For locally advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma that has not been treated before**, in patients with ECOG performance status 0 to 2.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '4427 Bladder/Urothelial locally advanced or metastatic enfortumab vedotin and pembrolizumab (eviQ ID 4427, version 1)', first approved 5 November 2025; review due 31 December 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/4427, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Do not use with** existing neuropathy of grade 2 or worse, uncontrolled diabetes, or active keratitis or corneal ulcers.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '4427 Bladder/Urothelial locally advanced or metastatic enfortumab vedotin and pembrolizumab (eviQ ID 4427, version 1)', first approved 5 November 2025; review due 31 December 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/4427, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Discuss with an expert first if the patient has** significant autoimmune disease, an organ transplant, past viral hepatitis or previous lung irradiation.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '4427 Bladder/Urothelial locally advanced or metastatic enfortumab vedotin and pembrolizumab (eviQ ID 4427, version 1)', first approved 5 November 2025; review due 31 December 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/4427, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Start only under specialists experienced with immunotherapy** who are confident they can manage immune-related adverse events.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '4427 Bladder/Urothelial locally advanced or metastatic enfortumab vedotin and pembrolizumab (eviQ ID 4427, version 1)', first approved 5 November 2025; review due 31 December 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/4427, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **The pivotal trial enrolled only patients who could have had platinum chemotherapy and immunotherapy.**
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '4427 Bladder/Urothelial locally advanced or metastatic enfortumab vedotin and pembrolizumab (eviQ ID 4427, version 1)', first approved 5 November 2025; review due 31 December 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/4427, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Regimen:** enfortumab vedotin 1.25 mg/kg IV on days 1 and 8 (capped at 125 mg, the maximum starting dose for patients of 100 kg or more) with pembrolizumab 200 mg IV on day 1, every 21 days. Continue until progression or unacceptable toxicity; pembrolizumab stops after at most 35 cycles, while enfortumab vedotin has no cycle limit.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '4427 Bladder/Urothelial locally advanced or metastatic enfortumab vedotin and pembrolizumab (eviQ ID 4427, version 1)', first approved 5 November 2025; review due 31 December 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/4427, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Pembrolizumab may instead be given as 400 mg every 42 days.**
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '4427 Bladder/Urothelial locally advanced or metastatic enfortumab vedotin and pembrolizumab (eviQ ID 4427, version 1)', first approved 5 November 2025; review due 31 December 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/4427, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Infusion order:** in cycle 1, leave 30 minutes between finishing enfortumab vedotin and starting pembrolizumab; if cycle 1 goes well, the gap can drop to 15 minutes.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '4427 Bladder/Urothelial locally advanced or metastatic enfortumab vedotin and pembrolizumab (eviQ ID 4427, version 1)', first approved 5 November 2025; review due 31 December 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/4427, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Enfortumab vedotin dose levels:** start 1.25 mg/kg (to 125 mg); first reduction 1.0 mg/kg (to 100 mg); second 0.75 mg/kg (to 75 mg); third 0.5 mg/kg (to 50 mg).
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '4427 Bladder/Urothelial locally advanced or metastatic enfortumab vedotin and pembrolizumab (eviQ ID 4427, version 1)', first approved 5 November 2025; review due 31 December 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/4427, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Pembrolizumab dose reduction is not recommended;** toxicity is managed by holding or stopping it. Moderate to severe hepatic impairment has not been studied.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '4427 Bladder/Urothelial locally advanced or metastatic enfortumab vedotin and pembrolizumab (eviQ ID 4427, version 1)', first approved 5 November 2025; review due 31 December 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/4427, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Enfortumab vedotin has caused severe and fatal skin toxicity and hyperglycaemia.**
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '4427 Bladder/Urothelial locally advanced or metastatic enfortumab vedotin and pembrolizumab (eviQ ID 4427, version 1)', first approved 5 November 2025; review due 31 December 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/4427, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Skin reactions are more frequent with the combination than with enfortumab vedotin alone.** Watch closely during the first 2 cycles and throughout, and refer to dermatology early.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '4427 Bladder/Urothelial locally advanced or metastatic enfortumab vedotin and pembrolizumab (eviQ ID 4427, version 1)', first approved 5 November 2025; review due 31 December 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/4427, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Suspected SJS/TEN, blistering, recurrent grade 3 or any grade 4 skin reaction: hold treatment at once and refer to a specialist; stop permanently if confirmed.**
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '4427 Bladder/Urothelial locally advanced or metastatic enfortumab vedotin and pembrolizumab (eviQ ID 4427, version 1)', first approved 5 November 2025; review due 31 December 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/4427, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Hyperglycaemia and diabetic ketoacidosis, sometimes fatal, occur even without known diabetes**; risk is higher with prior hyperglycaemia or BMI of 30 or more. Refer anyone with baseline HbA1c above 6.5% for glucose optimisation before cycle 1.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '4427 Bladder/Urothelial locally advanced or metastatic enfortumab vedotin and pembrolizumab (eviQ ID 4427, version 1)', first approved 5 November 2025; review due 31 December 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/4427, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Hold treatment until blood glucose is below 13.9 mmol/L.** Ketoacidosis needs urgent inpatient care.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '4427 Bladder/Urothelial locally advanced or metastatic enfortumab vedotin and pembrolizumab (eviQ ID 4427, version 1)', first approved 5 November 2025; review due 31 December 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/4427, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Pneumonitis/ILD, including deaths, is more common with the combination** (median onset 4 months). Grade 2: hold until grade 1 or less, reduce if it persists or recurs. Grade 3 or 4: stop.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '4427 Bladder/Urothelial locally advanced or metastatic enfortumab vedotin and pembrolizumab (eviQ ID 4427, version 1)', first approved 5 November 2025; review due 31 December 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/4427, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Check for neuropathy before every dose.** Grade 2: pause until grade 1 or less, resume at the same dose the first time and one level lower the second. Grade 3 or 4: stop.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '4427 Bladder/Urothelial locally advanced or metastatic enfortumab vedotin and pembrolizumab (eviQ ID 4427, version 1)', first approved 5 November 2025; review due 31 December 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/4427, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Eyes:** dry eye is the usual problem. Consider prophylactic artificial tears, refer to ophthalmology if symptoms persist or worsen, and note that contact lenses raise keratopathy risk.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '4427 Bladder/Urothelial locally advanced or metastatic enfortumab vedotin and pembrolizumab (eviQ ID 4427, version 1)', first approved 5 November 2025; review due 31 December 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/4427, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Bloods:** FBC, EUC, eGFR, LFTs, cortisol, thyroid function, glucose and HbA1c at baseline; FBC, EUC, eGFR, LFTs and glucose before every cycle; thyroid function every 4–6 weeks on treatment and 12-weekly afterwards.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '4427 Bladder/Urothelial locally advanced or metastatic enfortumab vedotin and pembrolizumab (eviQ ID 4427, version 1)', first approved 5 November 2025; review due 31 December 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/4427, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Screen for hepatitis before starting a checkpoint inhibitor**; chronic hepatitis B or C or uncontrolled HIV needs close monitoring and antivirals where indicated.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '4427 Bladder/Urothelial locally advanced or metastatic enfortumab vedotin and pembrolizumab (eviQ ID 4427, version 1)', first approved 5 November 2025; review due 31 December 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/4427, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Phase III evidence:** 886 patients with untreated advanced urothelial cancer were randomised to enfortumab vedotin plus pembrolizumab or to gemcitabine with cisplatin or carboplatin.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '4427 Bladder/Urothelial locally advanced or metastatic enfortumab vedotin and pembrolizumab (eviQ ID 4427, version 1)', first approved 5 November 2025; review due 31 December 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/4427, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Survival roughly doubled:** median overall survival 31.5 vs 16.1 months (HR 0.47) and median PFS 12.5 vs 6.3 months (HR 0.45), with benefit in every subgroup.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '4427 Bladder/Urothelial locally advanced or metastatic enfortumab vedotin and pembrolizumab (eviQ ID 4427, version 1)', first approved 5 November 2025; review due 31 December 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/4427, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **More treatment changes for toxicity with the combination:** dose reductions 40.7% vs 35.0% and discontinuations 37.9% vs 18.5%; treatment-related deaths were under 1.0% in both arms.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '4427 Bladder/Urothelial locally advanced or metastatic enfortumab vedotin and pembrolizumab (eviQ ID 4427, version 1)', first approved 5 November 2025; review due 31 December 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/4427, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **SEOM–SOGUG calls enfortumab vedotin with pembrolizumab the preferred first-line standard.** Its benefit held whatever the cisplatin eligibility, PD-L1 status, metastatic site or tumour location; 67.7% responded, 29.1% completely. It beat a control arm in which 30% had avelumab maintenance.
claims.locator: Spanish Society of Medical Oncology (SEOM) and Spanish Genitourinary Oncology Group (SOGUG), Clinical and Translational Oncology 27(11):4142-4159 (doi 10.1007/s12094-025-04045-2), 'SEOM–SOGUG clinical guideline for urothelial cancer (2025)', published 17 September 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12559142/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Longer follow-up (median 29.1 months):** at 24 months 37.1% against 12.6% were progression-free and 60.1% against 35.4% alive, and responses lasted a median of nearly 2 years.
claims.locator: Spanish Society of Medical Oncology (SEOM) and Spanish Genitourinary Oncology Group (SOGUG), Clinical and Translational Oncology 27(11):4142-4159 (doi 10.1007/s12094-025-04045-2), 'SEOM–SOGUG clinical guideline for urothelial cancer (2025)', published 17 September 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12559142/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Platinum chemotherapy:** cisplatin regimens (MVAC, dose-dense MVAC, cisplatin-gemcitabine) give median survival of 12–15 months. About 50% of patients cannot have cisplatin; carboplatin with gemcitabine is safer but less effective (median survival 9–10 months).
claims.locator: Spanish Society of Medical Oncology (SEOM) and Spanish Genitourinary Oncology Group (SOGUG), Clinical and Translational Oncology 27(11):4142-4159 (doi 10.1007/s12094-025-04045-2), 'SEOM–SOGUG clinical guideline for urothelial cancer (2025)', published 17 September 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12559142/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Avelumab maintenance after platinum:** for patients free of progression after 4–6 cycles, switching to avelumab lengthened median survival to 21.4 from 14.3 months (HR 0.69), with benefit across subgroups whether cisplatin or carboplatin had been used.
claims.locator: Spanish Society of Medical Oncology (SEOM) and Spanish Genitourinary Oncology Group (SOGUG), Clinical and Translational Oncology 27(11):4142-4159 (doi 10.1007/s12094-025-04045-2), 'SEOM–SOGUG clinical guideline for urothelial cancer (2025)', published 17 September 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12559142/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Nivolumab with cisplatin-gemcitabine (CheckMate 901):** for cisplatin-eligible patients, up to six cycles with nivolumab then nivolumab maintenance for at most 2 years raised median survival to 21.7 from 18.9 months (HR 0.78); 21.7% had a complete response. It is the only checkpoint inhibitor shown to add survival to first-line cisplatin chemotherapy.
claims.locator: Spanish Society of Medical Oncology (SEOM) and Spanish Genitourinary Oncology Group (SOGUG), Clinical and Translational Oncology 27(11):4142-4159 (doi 10.1007/s12094-025-04045-2), 'SEOM–SOGUG clinical guideline for urothelial cancer (2025)', published 17 September 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12559142/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **A single checkpoint inhibitor** is an option only for frail, platinum-ineligible patients with PD-L1-positive, preferably low-volume disease; single-arm trials gave response rates of 23.5% (atezolizumab) and 28.6% (pembrolizumab).
claims.locator: Spanish Society of Medical Oncology (SEOM) and Spanish Genitourinary Oncology Group (SOGUG), Clinical and Translational Oncology 27(11):4142-4159 (doi 10.1007/s12094-025-04045-2), 'SEOM–SOGUG clinical guideline for urothelial cancer (2025)', published 17 September 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12559142/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **After enfortumab vedotin with pembrolizumab there is no evidence for the next step.** The preferred choice is platinum chemotherapy, with no avelumab maintenance to follow; erdafitinib is reasonable when FGFR2/3 is altered.
claims.locator: Spanish Society of Medical Oncology (SEOM) and Spanish Genitourinary Oncology Group (SOGUG), Clinical and Translational Oncology 27(11):4142-4159 (doi 10.1007/s12094-025-04045-2), 'SEOM–SOGUG clinical guideline for urothelial cancer (2025)', published 17 September 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12559142/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **After platinum chemotherapy alone:** pembrolizumab improved survival over second-line chemotherapy (median 10.1 against 7.2 months, HR 0.71).
claims.locator: Spanish Society of Medical Oncology (SEOM) and Spanish Genitourinary Oncology Group (SOGUG), Clinical and Translational Oncology 27(11):4142-4159 (doi 10.1007/s12094-025-04045-2), 'SEOM–SOGUG clinical guideline for urothelial cancer (2025)', published 17 September 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12559142/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **After both platinum and a checkpoint inhibitor:** enfortumab vedotin alone (median survival 12.88 against 8.97 months, HR 0.70) or, for FGFR3/2 mutations or fusions, erdafitinib (12.1 against 7.8 months, HR 0.64). The best order of the two is unknown; taxanes or vinflunine later are for selected patients only.
claims.locator: Spanish Society of Medical Oncology (SEOM) and Spanish Genitourinary Oncology Group (SOGUG), Clinical and Translational Oncology 27(11):4142-4159 (doi 10.1007/s12094-025-04045-2), 'SEOM–SOGUG clinical guideline for urothelial cancer (2025)', published 17 September 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12559142/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Upper tract urothelial carcinoma:** treat advanced disease as for bladder cancer; it carries FGFR mutations more often than bladder tumours do.
claims.locator: Spanish Society of Medical Oncology (SEOM) and Spanish Genitourinary Oncology Group (SOGUG), Clinical and Translational Oncology 27(11):4142-4159 (doi 10.1007/s12094-025-04045-2), 'SEOM–SOGUG clinical guideline for urothelial cancer (2025)', published 17 September 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12559142/, retrieved 2026-09-24
